---
title: "Before you begin"
---

Welcome to **Getting Started with DNAnexus: R and JupyterLab**.

This short, self-paced tutorial will introduce you to the DNAnexus workflow used for MCPS research and training.

By the end of the tutorial, you will have started an R environment in DNAnexus, worked with synthetic training data, saved your analysis, ended your computing session, and returned later to confirm that your work was preserved.

::: {.callout-note title="How long will this take?"}
Allow approximately **20–25 minutes** to complete the tutorial.

We recommend completing the tutorial in one sitting so that you can practise the complete workflow from starting JupyterLab to safely ending your session.
:::

## What you need

Before starting, make sure that:

1. you have a working **DNAnexus account**; and
2. you have been given access to an **MCPS DNAnexus project**.

You do **not** need to create a DNAnexus project yourself.

You will normally have **Contributor** access to the project. This gives you the access needed to complete the tutorial and run analyses in JupyterLab.

::: {.callout-tip title="No command line experience required"}
You will complete the core workflow using the **DNAnexus graphical interface, JupyterLab, and R**.

You do not need to use a terminal or learn the DNAnexus command-line interface.
:::

## Which situation applies to you?

You may be completing this tutorial in one of two situations.

### I am attending an MCPS workshop

You have been given access to a **workshop project**.

The instructors will have created a folder for you at the top level of the project. It may look something like:

```text
participant-xx/
```

Use the participant folder assigned to you for your own notebooks and other work.

### I am working on an MCPS research project

You have been given access to a project containing MCPS research data.

MCPS research projects normally contain folders called:

```text
Data/
Users/
```

Inside `Users/`, there will usually be a folder bearing your name.

For example:

```text
Users/
├── Researcher A/
├── Researcher B/
└── Researcher C/
```

We recommend using your named folder inside `Users/` for your own notebooks and other work.

How you organise your own analysis files within this area is ultimately up to you.

## What do we mean by "your workspace"?

To keep the instructions simple, this tutorial uses the term **your workspace**.

::: {.callout-note title="Your workspace"}
In this tutorial, **your workspace** simply means the folder where you will keep your own notebook and other work.

It is not a special type of DNAnexus folder.

- **Workshop:** your workspace is the `participant-XX/` folder assigned to you.
- **Research project:** we recommend using your named folder inside `Users/` as your workspace.
:::

From this point onwards, the tutorial will simply refer to **your workspace**. The DNAnexus and JupyterLab steps are the same in both situations.

## The onboarding folder

Your project should also contain a shared folder called:

```text
mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/
```

This folder contains the files used for this tutorial.

Its contents will look broadly like:

```text
mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/
├── data/
│   └── example_data.csv
└── materials/
```

The `data/` folder contains **synthetic training data**.

The `materials/` folder can contain other shared resources used for the tutorial.

::: {.callout-important title="Two different places — two different purposes"}
**Your workspace** is where you keep **your own work**.

`mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/` contains **shared training resources**.

Do not save your own notebooks or outputs inside `mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/`.
:::

## A note about data safety

If you are completing this tutorial from a real MCPS research project, you may also be able to see folders containing real research data.

**You do not need to use or open those data to complete this tutorial.**

All exercises use the synthetic data supplied in:

```text
mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/data/
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Individual-level research data must remain in DNAnexus"}
**Never download individual-level MCPS research data to your local computer or another device.**

Individual-level MCPS research data must remain within the approved DNAnexus environment.

Later in the tutorial, we will distinguish between research data and analytical outputs that may be appropriate to download.
:::

## How this tutorial works

You will use two things side by side:

1. **this tutorial**, which explains what to do and why; and
2. a small **`getting-started.ipynb` DNAnexus Notebook**, where you will practise the workflow yourself.

Your copy of `getting-started.ipynb` will be provided in **your workspace**.

You do not need to memorise every step. A quick-reference page is provided at the end of the tutorial.

## Before you continue

Make sure that you can identify these two locations in your project:

| Location | What it is for |
|---|---|
| **Your workspace** | Your notebook and your own work |
| `mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/` | Shared synthetic data and training resources |

::: {.callout-tip title="Once you know these two locations, the two pathways merge"}
It does not matter whether you are using a workshop project or a research project.

From the next page onwards, the core DNAnexus workflow is the same.
:::

## Ready?

Next, we will look at the one DNAnexus concept that makes the rest of the workflow much easier to understand:

**your DNAnexus project is persistent, while your JupyterLab computing environment is temporary.**
